report:
Your assessment aligns with the current body of high-quality evidence: **ivermectin does not reduce mortality in COVID-19**.

**Key evidence:**

- **TOGETHER trial** (Brazil, published in *NEJM*, 2022) — a large, well-conducted randomized controlled trial found ivermectin did not reduce hospitalization or improve outcomes in COVID-19 outpatients compared with placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).

- **ACTIV-6 trial** (U.S., published in *JAMA*, 2022–2023) — a large platform RCT tested both standard and higher (600 μg/kg) doses of ivermectin against placebo in outpatients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19. Neither dose improved time to recovery or reduced hospitalization/death; the authors concluded findings "do not support the use of ivermectin" for COVID-19 (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827, https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2797483).

- **Cochrane systematic review** (updated 2022), the gold-standard for evidence synthesis, examined all available RCTs and concluded: "We found no evidence to support the use of ivermectin for treating COVID-19 or preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection," while noting the evidence base remains limited (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19).

- **WHO** reviewed the evidence and stated it is inconclusive, recommending ivermectin be used only within clinical trials rather than as standard treatment (https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-advises-that-ivermectin-only-be-used-to-treat-covid-19-within-clinical-trials).

**Conclusion:** Earlier positive signals largely came from smaller, lower-quality, or flawed/fraudulent studies. The largest, most rigorous RCTs (TOGETHER, ACTIV-6) and independent evidence syntheses (Cochrane, WHO) consistently show no mortality or hospitalization benefit from ivermectin in COVID-19. Your skepticism is well-supported by current evidence.
